test: a rapid move to zero with a trailing comment naming a different move is still a rapid move to zero [gcode.comment-cannot-change-command]
given: a rapid move to zero whose trailing comment mentions a different move
then: a rapid move to zero with a trailing comment naming a different move is still a rapid move to zero
why: the worst shape of the defect turned a rapid-to-zero into a full-speed move to a far target

test: a program made only of comment lines produces no motion [gcode.comment-lines-emit-nothing]
given: a program consisting only of comment lines
then: a program made only of comment lines produces no motion
why: a comment that produced a move would be a rapid to an unintended target

test: a pause command produces exactly one pause, with its duration kept in milliseconds without conversion [gcode.dwell-carries-milliseconds]
given: a pause command with a duration
then: a pause command produces exactly one pause, with its duration kept in milliseconds without conversion

test: an absolute move has the gauge length added, so a target on the sample becomes a position on the machine [gcode.gauge-offsets-absolute-moves]
given: a move to an absolute position, with a non-zero gauge length configured
then: an absolute move has the gauge length added, so a target on the sample becomes a position on the machine

test: a trailing comment on a move line does not change the target position the author wrote [gcode.move-ignores-trailing-comment]
given: a move line with a trailing comment containing a coordinate token
then: a trailing comment on a move line does not change the target position the author wrote
why: fixes a defect where "G1 X10 F5 ; X50 fast" moved to X50

test: a relative move is not offset by the gauge length, because it is a distance rather than a destination [gcode.relative-moves-are-not-offset]
given: a move by a relative distance, with a non-zero gauge length configured
then: a relative move is not offset by the gauge length, because it is a distance rather than a destination

test: a trailing comment on a waveform command does not change the amplitude the author wrote [gcode.waveform-ignores-comment]
given: a waveform command with a trailing comment mentioning an amplitude
then: a trailing comment on a waveform command does not change the amplitude the author wrote

given: the emergency-stop power line reporting lost power, with everything else healthy
then: lost power in the emergency-stop circuit is reported as the power fault, not as a tripped switch
why: the four emergency-stop reasons send the operator to different places, so the wrong one sends them to the wrong place with the machine still down

given: each of the eight fault sources tripped in turn, with every other input healthy
then: every fault source, tripped on its own, is reported under its own name and leaves the machine disabled with motion off
why: the reported reason is what the operator reads to diagnose a machine that will not move, and each one points at a different part of the machine

given: motion enabled with no faults, tripping one limit at a time from a fresh start
then: each physical limit on its own, whether frame tension, either travel endstop or an open door, puts the machine into the restricted state and is named as the reason
why: each limit is wired into the state machine separately, so one never connected would let the crosshead run at full speed into the frame with nothing reported

given: a stopped core and an open door together, after the operator has enabled motion
then: a fault holds the machine disabled even when a limit is also reached, and the fault is what gets reported
why: the restricted state only caps speed, so a restriction outranking a fault would keep the crosshead pulling while something was known to be broken

given: each neighbouring pair of causes in that order tripped at the same time, in turn
then: the fault reported follows one fixed order: a stopped core, then a stalled watchdog, then the emergency-stop inputs, then the drive, then the load cell
why: causes near the front produce the ones behind them, since a dead core also stops the drive answering, so this order makes the reported reason the root cause rather than a symptom

given: a stopped core, a stalled watchdog and an unresponsive load cell together
then: when several faults are active at once, the machine reports the highest-priority one rather than the most recent

given: the upper endstop reached and the door open together, with motion enabled
then: when several limits are reached at once, the machine reports the highest-priority one rather than the most recent

given: machine force at the configured maximum, then one unit above
then: force exactly at the maximum machine tension does not restrict motion, but one unit above it does

given: an operator enabling motion on a clean machine, then nothing about the machine changing
then: enabling motion latches: the machine holds manual mode while nothing is faulted, no limit is reached and no test is running

given: motion enabled on a clean machine with no test running
then: in manual mode the machine permits motion at full speed, not the reduced speed of the restricted state

given: a fault-free machine sitting disabled, with motion checked before and after the next control update
then: a request to enable motion is accepted at once, but motion stays off until the next control update
why: that same update re-reads the cores, the load cell, the endstops and the door, so an accepted request can never move the machine without a fresh safety check

given: a just-started machine with no faults, motion never enabled, and the door open
then: with motion never enabled, an open door leaves the machine disabled rather than restricted
why: the restricted state still lets the crosshead move, so a limit reached must never be what brings the machine out of disabled

given: a freshly started machine with every input healthy and nobody having asked for motion
then: a healthy machine stays disabled and allows no motion at all until an operator enables it
why: a crosshead that armed itself the moment everything looked healthy could start pulling with an operator's hands in the frame

given: the drive that moves the crosshead no longer reporting that it is ready
then: a motor drive that stops reporting itself ready is reported as a drive communication fault
why: the closed-loop changeover shipped asking the idle stepper instead of the active servo, so the machine booted into this fault and sat disabled

given: each fault source tripped on its own, with the operator then asking to enable motion
then: any single active fault makes the machine refuse a request to enable motion and stay disabled

given: a freshly started controller with nothing tripped, stalled or unresponsive
then: a machine with every core running, the watchdog alive and both the drive and the load cell answering reports no fault
why: every other fault test trips an input first, so this is the only one that would catch a ready signal read with its polarity inverted

given: the door endstop reporting open while motion is enabled
then: an open door puts the machine into the restricted state and is named as the reason
why: the door is the last limit the controller checks, so a check stopping one short would leave the machine at full speed with the guard open

given: a stopped core, a request to enable motion made while that fault stands, then the core healthy again
then: a request to enable motion refused because of a fault is discarded rather than queued until the fault clears
why: a request that survived the fault would start the crosshead the instant it cleared, with nobody having asked at that moment

given: motion enabled with no fault, then the door reporting open
then: the restricted state caps crosshead speed rather than stopping motion altogether
why: a limit is something the operator still has to drive back off, so cutting motion would strand the crosshead against it

given: a test already running with motion enabled, then the lower endstop reached
then: an endstop reached part-way through a test puts the machine into the restricted state rather than leaving it in the test state
why: the restricted state caps speed, so if a running test outranked the limit the crosshead would keep pulling at full test speed

given: tension above the frame maximum with both endstops and the door open; then tension back in range; then only the lower endstop and the door
then: when several limits are reached at once the machine names the highest-ranked one: frame tension, then the upper endstop, then the lower endstop, then the door
why: only one reason is reported at a time, and when the top condition clears the next one down takes over rather than the reason going blank

given: a healthy machine with motion enabled and a test reported as running
then: a running test keeps motion enabled at full speed, not the reduced speed of the restricted state
why: a tensile test is only valid at the programmed rate, so silently capping the speed would distort the measured curve instead of visibly stopping the machine

given: a test under way with the sample past both its force and its extension limit at once
then: with a sample over both its force and extension limits, the extension limit is reported as the reason for the restriction
why: the two trip together as a specimen yields, so the reason shown to the operator has to be a fixed choice rather than whichever was checked last

given: a test running with motion enabled, the sample past its extension limit, and frame tension low
then: a sample stretched past its configured extension limit during a test restricts the machine and is named as the reason
why: this check sat commented out alongside the sample force limit until both were restored

given: a test under way, the sample over its own force limit, and machine force reading near zero
then: a sample pulled past its own force limit during a test restricts the machine, even with frame tension far below its maximum
why: this check sat commented out of the state machine, so a running test could pull a specimen past the operator's configured limit with nothing reacting

given: motion enabled with no test running, and the sample past both its force and extension limits
then: a sample past its own force and extension limits does not restrict the machine unless a test is running
why: a specimen left gripped past its limits would otherwise hold the machine speed-limited while the operator jogs the crosshead to unload it

given: the controller starting up
then: the machine starts disabled with motion off, taking its maximum tension from the stored machine profile

given: a machine under manual control with motion enabled, and an operator request to stop motion
then: a request to stop motion is never refused, and leaves the machine disabled with motion off on the next update
why: a request to enable motion can be turned down by an active fault, but the stop path has no such gate

given: one of the cores no longer reporting that it is running
then: a processor core that stops running is reported as a core fault
why: the motion and monitoring loops run on separate cores; one dying silently would leave the machine moving unsupervised

given: a machine settled in manual control, then a test run starts
then: a test starting takes the machine out of manual control and into the test state

given: the load cell no longer reporting that it is ready
then: a load cell that stops answering is reported as a load cell fault, not as a drive fault
why: both the frame and the sample force limits are judged from the load cell, so a gauge gone quiet would leave the crosshead pulling against a stale reading

given: the watchdog reporting that a loop it supervises has stopped checking in
then: a supervised loop that stops checking in is reported as a watchdog fault, even with every processor core still running
why: a core counts as running even when the loop on it has wedged, so the check-in is the only thing that catches a stalled loop

given: a timer checked exactly at its deadline, and again one tick before it
then: a timer checked exactly at its deadline reports elapsed; checked one tick earlier, it does not

given: a multiply-then-divide whose intermediate exceeds 32 bits
then: a multiply-then-divide with an intermediate wider than 32 bits is computed exactly, and the sign is negative for an odd number of negative inputs
why: the P2 has no 64-bit divide; a 32-bit intermediate would silently wrap

given: the very first position report, whatever its absolute value
then: the first position report becomes the zero of extension, rather than being read as travel
why: the machine does not home to 0, so absolute position is not extension

given: travel smaller than the configured engagement slack
then: extension stays at zero until travel exceeds the engagement slack
why: the sample is not yet loaded, so reporting strain would be wrong

given: a machine whose tensile travel decreases machine position
then: on a machine whose tensile direction is decreasing position, moving to a smaller position produces positive extension
why: the DS2 gantry and the EdgeBoard gantry pull in opposite senses
